message.content: Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit). Read-only investigation only — no edits. CI just failed a Storybook accessibility (axe) check with this exact violation: ``` Element has insufficient color contrast of 2.95 (foreground color: #969696, background color: #ffffff, font size: 10.5pt (14px), font weight: normal). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1 ``` on `Was $595.00`, rendered by two stories: `Commerce/ZimmProductCardContent › WithSalePrice` and `Commerce/ZimmProductCard › WithSalePrice`. Both of these stories were added this session (recently) to close a coverage gap — nobody had ever added a story that actually sets `originalPrice` (triggering the "Was/Now" price display) before, so this may be a long-pre-existing styling bug in the underlying atom that simply never had a story exercising it, not a new regression from these specific story additions. Need to confirm that theory, not assume it. Investigate and report back: 1. **Find and read in full** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` and its theme recipe (likely `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` co-located, or a `theme/components/zimmProductPrice.ts` — find whichever actually exists). Identify exactly which part/prop produces the `data-testid= "product-was-price"` element, and exactly which token/value gives it its text colour. 2. **Resolve `#969696` to its source.** Is it a raw hardcoded hex literal in that recipe (which would also be a violation of this project's own `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` token-only styling rule, and should show up in `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`'s scan — run it and check), or does it come from a named foundation token (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts`)? If it's a token, name the exact token key and confirm its literal hex value matches `#969696` (or is close enough that browser rounding explains the gap). 3. **Git-blame / git-log** on whichever file actually sets this colour — confirm whether it was touched at all by any commit in the current branch's history (`git log --oneline -- ` restricted to this branch's own commits, i.e. commits after it diverged from `develop`) or whether it's fully untouched/pre-existing from the original SFCC-236 build. I want to know for certain whether this is a long-dormant bug or something this session's own edits changed. 4. **Compute or reason about what a compliant colour would actually be.** `#969696` on `#ffffff` is the failing pair. This project's foundation token file has a `grey` primitive scale and semantic aliases like `text.secondary`/`text.muted` etc (read `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts` in full to get the real list, don't guess). For each realistic candidate token this component might reasonably switch to, report its literal hex and note whether swapping to it is even a sensible design change (i.e. don't just find "the darkest grey" — check whether any candidate is already used elsewhere in this codebase for a secondary/muted/struck-through price-like treatment, which would make it a natural, low-risk choice, not an invented one). 5. **Check whether this same colour or the same recipe pattern is reused anywhere else** in the codebase (`grep -rn "969696\|#969696"` across `overrides/`, and separately grep for whatever token name you find in step 2, across `overrides/app/theme/` and `overrides/app/components/`) — I need to know the full blast radius before anyone picks a fix: does fixing this one recipe fix every place a shopper would see this problem, or are there other components with the identical colour choice that would still fail if someone looked? 6. **Check whether `.storybook/preview.tsx` runs axe as a hard failure or just a warning** (`a11y: {test: ...}` config) — I want to understand exactly why this specific check is what's blocking CI, to describe it accurately in a plan. 7. **Check `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`** for whatever file(s) you find need the colour value changed — report their exact protection tier and named owner, since that determines who needs to approve the eventual fix. Report findings as structured facts with exact file paths, line numbers, and literal values — I'm going to use this directly to write an execution plan, so precision matters more than narrative.

I have gathered comprehensive, verified evidence for all seven questions. Here is the structured report.

## 1. The atom, its recipe, and the failing element

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx`** (158 lines, read in full):
- Line 5: recipe key `const ZIMM_PRODUCT_PRICE_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductPrice';`
- Line 85: `const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_PRICE_RECIPE, { variant });` where `variant = isLoading || originalPrice ? 'sale' : 'default'` (line 80)
- Line 140: `<chakra.span __css={styles.wasPrice} data-testid="product-was-price">` — this is the exact element in the violation. It only renders inside the `originalPrice ? (...) : currentPrice` branch (line 137), i.e. only when a caller supplies `originalPrice` (the Was/Now sale treatment, PRC‑09).
- Line 149 is its sibling, `data-testid="product-now-price"`, styled by `styles.nowPrice`.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/zimmProductPrice.css.ts`** (71 lines, read in full) — the co-located Chakra multi-part recipe (`parts: ['container','wasPrice','nowPrice']`):
- Lines 45–64, the `sale` variant. Line 59: `wasPrice: { color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)' }` — this is the one line that paints `product-was-price`'s text colour.
- Lines 38–44 already contain an inline docblock stating exactly this trade-off: *"wasPrice → alias/color/text/subtlest (#969696) = text.muted / grey[300], 2.96:1 on white. Below the 4.5:1 AA threshold — a considered call by the FE lead to match the design system, logged here so it isn't mistaken for drift."*

## 2. `#969696` resolves to a named token, not a hardcoded literal

Chain (all read in full):
- `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:59` → `var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:50` → `'--zimm-color-text-muted': colors.text.muted,`
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:68` → `muted: grey[300],`
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:13` → `300: '#969696',`

So it is a genuine semantic-alias token (`text.muted`), not a raw hex literal in the recipe. Manually computing WCAG relative luminance for `#969696` on `#ffffff` gives **2.958:1** — matching the recipe's own "2.96:1" comment and explaining axe's reported "2.95" as trivial rounding, not a different value. There is no gap to explain: it's exactly this token, exactly this hex.

**`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`** — ran it. Output: **1 unacknowledged violation**, `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20 '59.125em'` — unrelated to this bug. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` does not appear at all, acknowledged or not, because `var(--zimm-color-text-muted)` is already a token reference — the script only flags raw literals bypassing the token system. It is structurally incapable of catching "uses a real token that happens to fail contrast," so its clean run here is not evidence of no problem, just evidence of a different rule being satisfied.

Also note `colour.ts:63–65`'s own comment: *"Handover contradicts itself here: tokens/colors.css says #969696 'confirmed', but tokens.md and contract/zimm-contract.js say #939393 and still flag it unresolved."* — a second, pre-existing open question about this same token's source-of-truth value, unrelated to the contrast failure itself.

## 3. Git history — confirmed pre-existing, not touched this session

Branch: `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`, merge-base with `develop`: `a18c68b`.

```
git log --oneline a18c68b..HEAD -- .../zimmProductPrice.css.ts .../zimmProductPrice/index.tsx
→ c00743f feat(ui-kits): add isLive opt-out to ZimmProductPrice (SFCC-236)
```
That is the **only** branch commit touching either file, and its diff (`git show c00743f`) touches only `index.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, and `.claude/registry/components.md` — it does **not** touch `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` at all.

Full history of `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` shows the colour line was set by **`fd249e4` — "fix(pdp): apply Figma-confirmed token corrections to ZimmProductPrice recipe (SFCC-194)"** (Jersey Perez, 2026‑08‑29), confirmed via `git blame -L 55,65`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor fd249e4 a18c68b` returns true, and `git branch --contains fd249e4` lists `develop` — **this commit is fully inherited from `develop`, pre-existing SFCC-194 work, not part of this branch's own history.**

**Working theory (task premise) is disproved, not confirmed.** It is false that "nobody had ever added a story that actually sets `originalPrice` before." Evidence:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.stories.tsx`'s `OnSale` story (lines 24–34) already sets `originalPrice: '$795.00'` and carries `parameters: { a11y: { test: 'off' } }` (lines 30–32) with a comment citing the exact same 2.95:1 figure.
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx`'s `OnSale` story (lines 48–64) does the same.

## 4. Compliant colour candidates

Full `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts` read (114 lines). Relevant greys/text aliases:
```
grey: 900 #191919, 800 #282828, 700 #454545, 600 #666666, 500 #707070, 300 #969696 (=muted=inverseGrey), 200 #d1d1d1
text: default=grey900 #191919, secondary=grey600 #666666, muted=grey300 #969696, inverseGrey=grey300 #969696
```
Contrast on white, computed manually:
- `grey[300]` / `text.muted` `#969696` → **2.96:1** — fails (current value)
- `grey[600]` / `text.secondary` `#666666` → **5.75:1** — passes AA
- `grey[900]` / `text.default` `#191919` → far exceeds AA but is the same colour as ordinary body text — would visually erase the "muted/de-emphasized was-price" intent
- `text.inverseGrey` — same literal value as `text.muted` (`grey[300]`), so switching to it changes nothing numerically; it's aliased separately purely for use on dark backgrounds, not a distinct colour.

**`text.secondary` (`#666666`, `var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)`) is not an invented choice — it is already the established, in-codebase precedent for exactly this situation.** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeModal/zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts:14–15` states verbatim: *"Caption-weight consent/disclaimer copy — text.secondary (#666, 5.74:1 on white). text.muted (#969696) would fail WCAG AA 4.5:1 at 12px on the white modal panel."* — i.e., a different squad already faced this identical token-choice decision and picked `text.secondary` specifically because `text.muted` fails on white. That makes it the lowest-risk, most consistent candidate for this recipe too, not a novel pick.

## 6. `.storybook/preview.tsx` — hard failure, not a warning

This is the global default for every story; a story can override it locally (as the two pre-existing `OnSale` stories do, via `parameters: { a11y: { test: 'off' } }`), but the two new `WithSalePrice` stories do not, so they inherit `'error'`.

CI mechanics, confirmed in `.github/workflows/qa.yml` (Tier 1 frozen file — see below), job `storybook-test` (lines 385–421): runs on every PR to `develop`/`release/**`, gated by a path filter that includes `overrides/app/components/**` and `.storybook/**` (lines 88–94). It builds Storybook, serves it, then runs `node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006` (line 411). `--ci` combined with `a11y.test: 'error'` means any non-excluded axe violation makes this command exit non-zero and fails the job — this is the exact mechanism blocking CI, not a lint warning or soft check.
